messages:
Taylor (eng): Quick question from the all-hands: is the post-incident timeline for last week's cache outage up anywhere? I want the short version for the team standup.
Mira (SRE): Yes, posted: https://redwood.internal/rcas/INC-2026-047. Root cause: a rollout that inadvertently disabled KV prefix caching on a subset of nodes, causing increased backend load and elevated tail latency for 2.2 hours.
Anika (product): Can product get a 3-line summary we can paste into the customer-facing note?
Mira (SRE): Sure: "We experienced elevated latency due to a configuration rollout that disabled prefix caching on some serving nodes; mitigation restored cache settings and load returned to normal. Impact: increased latency for certain dedicated customers in eu-central for ~2.2 hours; no data loss."
Taylor (eng): What introduced the bad config? Was it human error or a deployment script?
Mira (SRE): Human error during a configdrift cleanup run. The cleanup script had a glob that matched both legacy and active config keys. Fix is to scope the glob and add a dry-run guard.
Lee (obs): For follow-ups: adding a metric alert for cache miss rate spike and an invariant check in the config-service. I filed an internal ticket: https://ops.redwood/tickets/TKT-889
Anika (product): Owner ask from leadership: who will own the customer note and what is the ETA? Also need distribution list.
Jamie (CEO): We also want a named owner for the prevention work and a date for when the config-service will block unsafe globs.
Mira (SRE): Owners: customer note 33 Anika (product) 33 ETA: 2026-03-28. Config guard 33 Taylor (eng) 33 ETA: 2026-04-05. Alerting and dashboards 33 Lee (obs) 33 ETA: 2026-03-31.
Taylor (eng): I'll add the guarded-glob change to the deploy pipeline. Example patch snippet I'm using in the config-service CI: 
```
# config_guard.py (unit)
def is_safe_glob(pattern):
    deny = ["*legacy*", "*deprecated*"]
    return not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(pattern, d) for d in deny)
```

Taylor (eng): I'll also add an automated dry-run that exits nonzero if the change would strip active keys.
Anika (product): opsbot, pull impacted customer list for eu-central dedicated pools so we can triage outreach.
incident-bot: Impact summary created: 9 affected accounts. Link: https://ops.redwood/impacts/INC-2026-047
Mira (SRE): Quick note: we've updated the internal postmortem with exact timeline + debug logs. If you're commenting on the doc, please add your note with initials and timestamp.
Lee (obs): Putting a dashboard tile in the console for prefix-cache-hit-rate per-pool, tagging @SRE for review.
Jamie (CEO): Thanks all. Please make sure the owners update the all-hands follow-up tracker after their PRs are merged. We'll review progress at next week's follow-up slot.
Taylor (eng): Will do. I'll link PRs here once the CI and dry-run are in.
Anika (product): Draft customer note ready, will post to #customer-comms for review by 5pm PT.
Mira (SRE): Final: if anyone changes ETA / owner, update the follow-up doc so we don't duplicate effort. Marking this thread as the canonical follow-up for INC-2026-047. :white_check_mark:
